sections.title: Key display (recording lessons)
sections.tags: keys keycast key display show pressed hotkeys combination mouse buttons wheel scroll middle record video lesson tutorial inspector
sections.body:
Inspector → Windows → the last button (key caps and a mouse): a small window that shows what is pressed — for recording lessons and showing hotkeys.

Keys and combinations — as key caps: Ctrl + Shift + K; the same again — ×N. A mouse button — a mouse with that button lit (left, right; the middle one — the wheel lit); the wheel rolled — an arrow up or down by it. With a modifier held: Alt + the mouse. The last few combinations stay small above.

Drag it anywhere — its place is kept; × (on hover) or the button again — closed. Left open, it opens again on the next start. ⚙ by the button — the background's opacity (0 % — the keys alone over the program) and the size.

sections.title: UV Sets and UV Mats
sections.tags: uv set sets mats material materials udim tile overlap head body texture manager pack
sections.body:
UV Set — a UV layout of its own over some polygons; a polygon can be in several (two layouts of a head), it shows the one picked last. UV Mats — the materials, each with its texture, each using a set.

A click on a set — its layout shown, only it in the UV Editor (again — all); on a mat — only its polygons, its set lit. Double click on a mat — its textures. F2 — rename.

＋ a new set over the selected polygons (their UV as they are) / a new mat; ⇲ the selected polygons into the picked set / given the picked mat; ⧉ duplicate a set — a second layout, edited on its own. Drag a set — its place: the higher one wins a merge. RMB → Merge with — one layout of both, the higher one's UV where they overlap. Alt + drag a set or a mat onto another — merged, the dragged one wins. Pack all / Unfold all put each mat into its own tile.

sections.title: The gizmo: its place, axes, Align
sections.tags: gizmo pivot alt free align axis plane vertex edges normal view world bake transform
sections.body:
Alt + drag a handle (or Free gizmo in the options) — the gizmo itself moved / turned, the model stays. In Object mode its place and axes go into the mesh's Transform; Bake puts the transform into the points and makes those axes the mesh's own.

Align: an axis (X / Y / Z) or a plane (XY / YZ / XZ — the axis square to it) turned: to the selected vertex (from the mesh's pivot; a plane — through the vertices), along the selected edges (a plane — through them), to the selection's normal, to the view, or World — the world's axes back.

sections.title: Help on a button (~)
sections.tags: help faq tilde backquote button tool description what does this do
sections.body: Point at any button, tool or menu item and press ~ — this FAQ opens at its description.

sections.title: Isolation (H)
sections.tags: isolate isolation hide show unhide h ring pie selection head working group
sections.body:
H taphide / show the selected (a component mode: the selected polygons)
H heldthe isolation ring: every function below — release towards one or click it
Ctrl+Hisolate the selection (picked polygroups first)
Shift+Hisolate the selection and the head
Ctrl+Shift+Hisolate the working group; a component mode — only the selected polygons
Unhide allevery hidden polygon / polygroup of the room shown

sections.title: Select Cursor and the selection kinds
sections.tags: select cursor rectangle lasso loop ring fill outline n-gons ngons double click pattern clear ctrl drag shift rmb ctrl rmb
sections.body:
Select Cursor: a click picks, a held LMB paints. A double click on a polygon — the whole piece; a click and a double click beside it — the loop; a double click further on — every so many along the loop (as far apart as the two). Ctrl + a stroke over empty space — everything deselected.

Rectangle, Lasso, Loop, Ring, Fill, Outline — the other kinds (Shift+RMB: the ring of kinds). Select N-gons — every polygon of more than four sides.

Ctrl+RMB — the edits of the selection (Mirror, Melt, Grow, Shrink, Hard / Soft edges, Split, Detach…). Del — the selected elements deleted (not the mesh).

sections.title: Brush
sections.tags: brush move smooth relax inflate shrink hardness radius symmetry
sections.body: LMB — as its mode (RMB — the modes: Move, Smooth, Relax, Inflate, Shrink). Shift — smooth, Shift+Ctrl — relax. Ctrl+RMB drag: ←→ radius, ↑↓ hardness; Ctrl+wheel — radius. With a selection only it is touched; with Symmetry only the side the stroke is on is brushed, the other follows.

sections.title: Slide
sections.tags: slide edge slide vertex slide proportional parallel
sections.body: Selects as the Select Cursor. A drag in empty space slides the selected vertices along their edges: LMB — proportionally (the same share of each edge), RMB — in parallel (the same distance).

sections.title: PolyPen
sections.tags: polypen pen draw polygon retopology anchors fill extrude weld
sections.body:
The element under it is lit; a held LMB drags it (a vertex let go on another — welded). Clicks draw a polygon: the first point again or a double click closes it, Esc drops it. From a vertex / an edge to another of the same polygon — the polygon cut; across a gap on the rim — the gap filled.

Ctrl + drag an edge — a polygon pulled out (onto another edge — the gap between them); Ctrl + drag a polygon — extruded; Ctrl + click — deleted. Shift + click — an anchor; Shift+RMB — the polygon of the points round the pointer. [ / ] — the fill radius; Ctrl+Shift held — Loop.

sections.title: Bridge
sections.tags: bridge connect two loops chains edges polygons
sections.body: A click: rows of polygons between two selected chains of edges (or the rims of two selections of polygons). Subdivision, Tension, Spin steps, Reverse, Keep original — in the options.

sections.title: Fill Hole
sections.tags: fill hole cap close quads tris fan ngon subdivision loops edge flow
sections.body: The hole nearest the pointer (or every hole the selection touches) is shown filled. LMB — fill; RMB — the next variant; the wheel — the kind: Quads, Quads + tris, Tris to a centre, Tris without a centre, N-gon. Shift+RMB drag — Edge Flow (the patch carries on the shape round it); Ctrl+RMB drag — Subdivision (loops inside it). After a fill the patch stays selected and these change it while it stays the selection.

sections.title: Bevel / Extrude
sections.tags: bevel extrude push out caps chamfer
sections.body: The selected polygons pushed out: drag sideways — how far. The bevel and its segments, the top / bottom caps and what is selected after — in the options (changing them makes the last extrude again).

sections.title: Inset
sections.tags: inset circle vertex circles
sections.body: The selected polygons' rim drawn in: drag sideways — how far (depth, segments, as a whole or each one — in the options). On vertices — a circle of so many sides round each one.

sections.title: Loop
sections.tags: loop cut insert edge loop ring cuts
sections.body: The cut across the ring of polygons under the pointer is shown. The wheel — how many; Shift — onto the 1/2, 1/4, 1/6… marks; Ctrl — parallel to the nearer side. LMB cuts, RMB cuts and selects the new edges.

sections.title: Knife
sections.tags: knife cut curve through
sections.body: Clicks on the mesh — the anchors of a smooth cut (Esc ends it, Enter cuts); a drag from empty space — a straight cut. Ctrl + drag — an anchor moved; Shift+RMB — cut, optimise, recompute, delete. Weld radius and Cut through — in the options.

sections.title: Plane Cut
sections.tags: plane cut slice split remove part
sections.body: Drag a line across the mesh — the plane through it, edge-on to the view. Cut all, Split, Remove part A / B, several cuts at a spacing, only the selection, the cuts selected — in the options.

sections.title: Weld
sections.tags: weld merge point pairs
sections.body: Select, then RMB: to a point (onto the vertex under the pointer, else their middle) or in pairs (two chains of edges, vertex by vertex).

sections.title: Collapse Edge
sections.tags: collapse edge merge vertex
sections.body: The selected edges each into a vertex; edges joined to each other — into one.

sections.title: Optimize
sections.tags: optimize clean weld duplicate vertices mid edge
sections.body: A click: vertices in one place welded (the distance — Ctrl+RMB drag, a circle; or the options; 0.1 mm), vertices in the middle of a side between two polygons taken out. The selection, else the whole mesh.

sections.title: Edge Shaper
sections.tags: edge shaper equal distance spacing edge flow flatten plane straighten
sections.body: Selects as the Select Cursor. Drag → in empty space: LMB — even spacing (the shape kept); RMB — Edge Flow; Shift+LMB — flat on a plane (the chain's ends on it; three vertices picked — their plane); Shift+RMB — straight.

sections.title: Smooth EdgeChain
sections.tags: edge chain curve smooth even
sections.body: Select edges, Shift+RMB — a curve they follow; drag its anchors, a click on it — a new anchor; smooth / even them in the options.

sections.title: Relax Mesh
sections.tags: relax smooth even out ctrl+r
sections.body: Ctrl+R — the selected vertices (none — all) evened out on the surface, the rim kept.

sections.title: Snap to the references
sections.tags: snap reference geometry surface project
sections.body: The selected vertices (none — all) put onto the reference meshes' surface (no reference — onto the other shown meshes).

sections.title: Normals
sections.tags: normals align reverse flip smooth hard copy rotate
sections.body: Align Normals — the selected polygons turned to face one way (each piece outward); Reverse Normals — turned round. The Normals tool shows them: a drag in empty space turns the selected ones; Smooth — the selection smooth with its border hard; Shift + click another mesh — its normals copied onto the selected polygons (none — all).

sections.title: Mirror
sections.tags: mirror symmetry radial kaleidoscope flower virtual symmetry group apply
sections.body:
A click — a copy of the selected polygons (none — the mesh) by the axis: the side it is on found by itself, the seam welded. Radial — copies round the axis; Radial mirror — each and its mirror; Radial half — round half of it. Axis, kind, copies — in the options.

Virtual symmetry group — the selected meshes into a group whose symmetry is only shown, in any place; on such a group the same button gives Apply (make it real), the kind, or removal.

sections.title: UV Seams and Sew
sections.tags: uv seams sew mark seam stitch unfold
sections.body: In the UV window: Seam — the selected edges become seams (where Unfold cuts); Sew — the UV joined along the selected edges, both sides' points brought together, the seam gone.

sections.title: UV of a character: the workflow
sections.tags: uv workflow character unwrap unfold pack seams symmetry face density check order
sections.body:
1. Sets — select objects or polygons, ＋ a UV Set (Head, Body, Cloth, Eyes…); set its texture size and padding in pixels next to it. Picking a set darkens the rest.

2. Seams — with Shift+X Symmetry on they go to both sides. Select edges, C. Hover a shell in 3D — its unfold is previewed in the editor.

3. Unfold — U / Shift+U. Symmetry on: a shell across the middle comes out symmetric, a pair (ears, hands) — one the mirror of the other; −X shells are shown burgundy.

4. Face — the lips' and eyes' rims: L open (points facing each other), Shift+L shut (to paint closed lids).

5. Shape — J grid, N line, I / Shift+I upright, the frame (E / R / T) to move, turn, scale.

6. Density — Alt+D take from a shell, Shift+D give; a shell's own × (the face ×2) in Pack.

7. Pack — Shift+B: by shape, at the padding, symmetric with Symmetry on; locked shells stay, groups lie together, alike shells stack.

8. Check — V to the problems, Select next to a count, fix, pack again. Or send it all to RizomUV.

sections.title: UV Editor hotkeys
sections.tags: uv keys hotkeys shortcuts keyboard editor
sections.body:
Turned on by ⌨ UV keys on the UV window's top. The Topology room's selection, view and gizmo keys stay as they are (Ctrl+A / D / I, F, H, B, E / R / T, Shift+X).

Seams: C seam (polygons — cut off into a shell), Shift+C off, Alt+C Auto (closed shells), W sew, Shift+W snap together.
Unfold: U, Shift+U all, Alt+U symmetric, O Optimize.
Face: L open, Shift+L shut, Alt+L off.
Shape: J grid, N line, I by edge, Shift+I upright, M / Shift+M mirror U / V, [ / ] turn, K / Shift+K stack / unstack.
Move: arrows — a texel (Shift — 10), Alt+arrows align, Alt+Shift+arrows space out.
Symmetry: Shift+X, Shift+Y Symmetrize, Alt+Y the axis.
Density: Alt+D take, Shift+D give.
Pack: Shift+B all, Alt+B the selected, Alt+H lock, G / Shift+G group / ungroup.
Pins: Alt+V / Alt+T straightened and pinned, Alt+Shift+C off.
Brushes: Alt+R Relax, Alt+P Pin, [ / ] size, Esc off.
View: V — plain → stretch by area → by angles → the problems.

sections.title: UV packing: lock, no turn, groups, shell density
sections.tags: uv pack lock locked turn rotate group groups density scale stack padding symmetric
sections.body:
Pack lays the shells by their outlines into the set's texture at its padding in pixels; with Symmetry on — shells across the middle on the axis, pairs mirrored, the rest in the gaps. Alike shells (eyes, buttons) stay stacked.

Each shell's own settings (the row under Pack): Lock (Alt+H) — left where it is, the rest packed round it, slate in the editor; No turn — never turned; Group (G) — laid close together, a colour per group; Shell density ×N — N times the texel density of the rest (Pack and Texel density Set keep it); Clear — all off. They are saved in the project and survive a new Unfold.

A shell with polygons in two UV Mats is packed once, with the mat most of it is in.

sections.title: UV of a face: lips and eyelids
sections.tags: uv face lips eyes eyelids lids mouth closed open paint
sections.body: Select the rim of the mouth or an eye (Edge mode: the loop round the hole) or the face shell itself (its holes are found), then L — Open: the upper and lower points stand straight across from each other; Shift+L — Shut: each upper point on its lower one, the hole zipped — the lids laid as if closed, to paint them. Alt+L — off. The pairs are kept by Unfold and Optimize; the rims are drawn orange (open) and amber (shut).

sections.title: UV check: overlaps, padding, density
sections.tags: uv check problems overlap flipped padding density asym mirror outside diagnostics
sections.body: The Check block counts, for the set's texture and each UV Mat's tile apart: turned over, over another (stacks don't count), past the tile, nearer than the padding, off the wanted texel density (or the median), a mirror pair not mirrored. Select — those polygons. Show the problems (or V in turn) tints them in the editor.

sections.title: UV brushes: Relax and Pin
sections.tags: uv brush relax pin pins smooth stretch brushes
sections.body:
Relax brush (Alt+R, the ≈ button): drag over the UV — the points under the circle are relaxed by SLIM, the rest of their shells held: the stretch evens out there, nothing turns over. The shell's border stays; with Shift it relaxes too, but never into an overlap. The lips' and eyelids' rims are always held.

Pin brush (Alt+P): drag over UV points — pinned (yellow dots); Ctrl — unpinned. Unfold lays the shell round the pinned points, Optimize and the Relax brush keep them; RizomUV gets them as pins.

[ / ] — the size, Shift+[ / ] — the strength, Esc or the button again — off. Only what the editor shows is touched.

sections.title: Auto seams for closed shells
sections.tags: uv auto seams closed sphere ball torus unfold cut
sections.body: A closed shell (a ball, a closed boot, a torus — no border) can't be unfolded as it is. Auto in Seams (Alt+C) gives it seams: its handles cut open, then a path between its two far ends — at the back (away from +Z), low, along sharp edges — and branches from it while the stretch keeps dropping. Unfold does this by itself to a closed shell and says so; the seams stay, move them and unfold again.

sections.title: Getting started
sections.tags: start begin basics overview workflow tutorial first steps new project how to start pipeline idea
sections.body:
The program models stylized (anime) hair: you draw curves on a reference head, NURBS surfaces (walls) are spanned between neighbouring curves, and the result is converted into a quad mesh and exported as OBJ.

Typical workflow

  • Import the head: + in the outliner → Head, or drop an OBJ / GLB / GLTF onto the window (see Import).
  • Draw curves with the Curve tool {k:draw}; group them per lock or per hair part.
  • Select 2 curves → Shift + RMB → wall between them; 3+ curves → volume lock (see Surfaces & locks).
  • Shape with the gizmo ({k:move} / {k:rotate} / {k:gizmo}) and the Brush {k:brush}; place guides {k:guide} where loops must follow a line.
  • Select the cocoons → the Convert to geometry window (right column) lists them → Convert (the meshes go straight into Meshes; Ctrl+Z — undo) → ⭳ Export (or ⇪ Send over a 🔗 Bridge).

Until conversion the hair is Live (rebuilt on every change); after it the topology is Baked into a mesh.

sections.title: How to: align / even out the mesh
sections.tags: align aligned alignment line up match even evenly uneven out spacing distribution flow straight straighten tidy clean up improve better nice fix topology mesh grid loops loop rows quads density dense sparse slanted diagonal crooked wavy neighbours neighbor locks join narrow strip y junction fork
sections.body:
Loops (the rows of the future mesh) are placed automatically; these tools change where they go. Most are in the Convert window (right column) and apply to the ticked groups.

Even spacing

  • Relax loop spacing — evens the distance between loops along every curve.
  • Loop step (Set reference) — the target distance; Match project loop step in group properties gives a group the project's step.
  • Deviation — how much a loop's size may differ from the step by the curvature (step 10, 50% → 5…15; 0 — the same everywhere).

Loop direction

  • Loops: horiz. ↔ perp. — 0: horizontal loops, 1: loops square to each lock.
  • Fix sharp angles (on by default) — loop edges are turned square to their walls; a narrow strip between close curves stays straight across, the slant goes into the wide walls; higher — more places, more strongly.
  • Y junctions — where two curves of a lock that ran together part (a fork inside the lock), a loop goes right through that anchor. Only these anchors place loops — how many anchors a curve has doesn't matter. In locks welded to other locks the shared trunks' loops rule instead (a loop of one lock alone would end on its neighbour's wall).
  • Guide Priority — in a guide's zone the guide wins over all of these (from 50% also over the Y junction loops).
  • Guides {k:guide} — a Line or a NURBS disc: loops follow it; Loop density, Influence radius, Priority set how strongly (see Guides).

Neighbouring locks

  • Every lock is built on its own: only its group's settings and the guides shape its loops — neighbouring locks (in its group or any other) don't. Parent groups are just folders.
  • Shift + click on a group's (or a cocoon's) fold arrow ▸ / ▾ — folds or unfolds its whole branch: every group and cocoon inside it too.
  • Locks welded along a trunk (curves sharing a segment, in any groups) share the very same loops there, one to one; past the fork each goes on its own.
  • A guide that should not shape some locks: its Excluded groups, or ⏻ to switch it off.

Also

  • Smooth, even curves give even loops — see How to: align / smooth a curve.
  • Check the result: Convert → look at the preview → Cancel, change, Convert again.

sections.title: How to: fix topology problems
sections.tags: fix repair topology problem problems broken bad mesh gap gaps crack tear slit hole holes open edges sliver thin narrow triangle triangles tris fan non-manifold nonmanifold overlap overlapping double twisted seam seams merge weld close cap
sections.body:
Gaps / cracks between walls

  • Curves that run together should be welded (drag an anchor onto another → Weld); then Merge shared trunks (Convert panel) makes them one surface.
  • A hole between curves: pie Fill the hole between these curves, or the Fill modifier for a whole group.
  • Two locks growing into each other: pie Unite locks (Y / X junction).
  • Open ends of closed locks: the Cap modifier.

Thin loops, fans of triangles, slanted loops

  • Near a guide: lower its Priority or Loop density, change its Influence radius, exclude the group (Excluded groups) or switch it off (⏻).
  • Relax loop spacing and Fix sharp angles (Convert panel) smooth out uneven loops; see How to: align / even out the mesh.
  • Wobbly curves make wobbly loops: Even out anchors, Smoothing (curve properties).

Checking

  • Convert shows a preview first — Confirm only when it looks right; Cancel brings the NURBS back.
  • {k:isolate} / {k:isolateGroup} isolate the problem lock to see it clearly; X-ray to look inside.

sections.title: How to: walls are not created between curves
sections.tags: surface surfaces wall walls nurbs not created no wall won't create cannot create can't make fails nothing happens missing broken curves lock copy duplicate delete weld merge anchors identical places
sections.body:
Sometimes the program won't make a NURBS surface (wall) between curves — e.g. after many welds, cuts and joins. Rebuild them from copies:

  1. Select those curves and make copies of them — {k:duplicate} (Duplicate).
  2. Delete the old curves (select them → Del).
  3. Select the copies → Shift + RMB → ▦ Create NURBS surface (2 curves), Walls between … curves or ◈ Volume lock (closed) (3+ curves).
  4. Select all the curves of the lock again → Shift + RMB → ⛓ Merge anchors at identical places — the anchors that lie on each other are welded (stitched) back together, as the old curves were.

sections.title: How to: turn a fork (Y junction)
sections.tags: fork forks y junction junctions branch branching split splits where curves meet meet join welded anchor three curves turn rotate flip swap which curve goes straight smooth through sharp corner crotch angle direction
sections.body:
Where two curves run together and then part, or a curve branches off another one, the shared anchor is a fork (a Y junction — the curves form a Y). Through a fork one pair of directions goes smoothly, the other curve leaves at a corner.

  1. Select the fork anchor (click it).
  2. Shift + RMB → ⤾ Rotate junction → pick Curve N — smooth through: that curve now passes through the fork smoothly, the others branch off it. For a curve that ends at the fork, picking it again tries the next direction.
  3. ↺ Automatic — back to the program's own choice.

sections.title: How to: align / smooth a curve
sections.tags: align straighten straight smooth smoother curve curves wobble wobbly wavy zigzag jagged kink corner sharp even out tidy clean fix curve anchors fewer simplify handles flatten line up symmetric mirror
sections.body:
• Smoothing (curve properties) — no curvature jumps; the anchors stay, the handles change.
  • Even out anchors — the anchors themselves move so the curve runs smoothly (takes out zigzag / wobble), the overall shape stays.
  • Roundness — 0: spline, 1: circle arcs through the anchors.
  • Brush {k:brush} with Shift — smooth by painting; with the curve selected only it is affected.
  • Pie (Shift + RMB): Optimize anchors (fewer anchors, same shape), Average curve, Recalculate handles, Delete anchor / keep shape.
  • B + LMB on an anchor — sharp ↔ smooth.
  • Straight along an axis: move anchors with the gizmo {k:move} and lock axes ({k:axisX} / {k:axisY} / {k:axisZ}); edit in a fixed view (Front / Side / Top in 🎥 Camera).
  • Left and right the same: group symmetry (group properties).

Several curves selected: Smoothing and Even out anchors apply to all of them.

sections.title: Viewport & camera
sections.tags: floor grid ground navigation navigate viewport camera view views change view orbit rotate view turn around pan move view zoom dolly frame focus perspective orthographic ortho front back left right side top split screen layout panes snap angle reset camera xray x-ray see through transparency isolate hide show

Navigation (like Cinema 4D)

Alt + LMB dragorbit around the last clicked point (no roll)
Alt + MMB / MMB dragpan
Alt + RMB drag / wheelzoom
Shift while orbitingsnap to the nearest standard angle (front, sides, ¾, top, bottom)
{k:frame}frame the selection (or everything); over the outliner — reveal the item there

Changing the view

  • 🎥 Camera ▾ (above the viewport): Reset camera, Perspective / Orthographic, fixed views Front / Back / Left / Right / Top (click, or drag a view into a pane). ⧉ Copy position — the camera's position and direction as one line of text (HMC-CAM …) in the clipboard, to send along with a screenshot; ⎘ Paste position — the camera goes back there.
  • Split screen: layouts 2, 2+1, 1+2, 4; swap panes by dragging them in the small scheme. The pane under the cursor is the active one.
  • {k:camMenu} — split screen on + camera menu at the cursor; press it twice quickly — back to the single view.
  • In the Top view Alt + LMB left / right turns the picture.
  • Floor (second row, right of Reference): the first slider moves the floor grid lower / higher, the second — its opacity (0 — off). Double-click — reset.

Seeing through

  • X-ray slider — how much curves, anchors and guides show through the head and the hair; also how see-through the surfaces are.
  • Top bar: show / hide and opacity of Anchors, Curves, Guides, Grid (surface grid), ◧ NURBS (surfaces), ⬢ Wire (imported meshes).
  • {k:hide} hide / show selected · {k:isolate} isolate the selection · {k:isolateHead} isolate + head · {k:isolateGroup} only the working group.
  • ◎ Solo (button next to Reference): {k:isolateGroup} that follows you — only the group you work in is shown, and selecting something in another group (in the outliner or the viewport) switches to that group. Nothing selected — the last group stays. {k:isolate}, {k:isolateHead} or {k:isolateGroup} (or the button again) switch Solo off — everything is shown.

sections.title: Files, projects & autosave
sections.tags: file files open save save as recent project projects hairmesh json load start screen autosave autosaves backup recovery restore crash unsaved drag drop drop file migrate migration presets preset export obj
sections.body:
📁 File window

Opens on start, with 📁 File and {k:open}.

  • Recent projects — cards with a preview; click to open, Open… for any file. ✕ removes a card from the list (the file stays).
  • Examples — finished hairstyles shipped with the program (opened on the very first start). An example opens as a copy: Save asks where to keep yours. The card in the corner of the viewport credits the author of the example's concept art, with a link to the original post.
  • Autosaves — the newest 5 copies from the autosave folder. Opening one doesn't change it; save the project to keep it.
  • Migrate — another project's hair (curves, surfaces, modifiers, with their groups) comes into this project as a new group. On top — Presets (see Presets).

Saving

  • {k:save} save (into the same file), {k:saveAs} save as. Projects are .hairmesh files; old .json projects open too.
  • ⏱ Autosave: every N minutes when something changed, into a chosen folder (by default the program's System\Autosaves), as name_autosave_1…K.hairmesh in turn.
  • Started from its shortcut, the program works with files through its launcher: the system's own Open / Save dialogs (they start in System\Projects), and the browser never asks for permission to use folders. A double-click on a .hairmesh file opens it in the program (in the open one, if it is running). Opened as a plain HTML file, the program uses the browser's dialogs and asks for permissions as before.
  • Recovery: the unsaved scene is kept in the browser once a minute; after a crash the program offers it back on start.
  • Cocoons (◍ in the left toolbar) — see-through shells round the locks that show their loops as rings: section Cocoons.
  • ⭳ Export ▾ (top bar) — writes the selected meshes (or the meshes in the selected groups, or all) as OBJ / PLY (quads) or glTF / STL (triangles), with a scale; convert the hair first (see Loops & conversion).
  • 🔗 Bridge ▾ — sends the meshes straight into another program: Blender (install the add-on from the panel) or Maya (drag its script into the viewport) live over a local port — objects of the same name are updated in place; or a Folder another program watches (Unreal, Unity, Godot auto-import; ZBrush, Cinema 4D…). Once set up, ⇪ Send next to it (Ctrl+Shift+E) sends with one click.

Drag & drop

Drop files onto the window: boxes appear — Open project, Migrate into this project, Import as head, Import as mesh. Pictures go to the reference board.

sections.title: Presets & migration
sections.tags: preset presets library save lock reuse template migrate migration merge combine another project bring in copy hair between projects folder create preset
sections.body:
• File → Migrate: pick a recent project (or Choose file…, or drop a file on Migrate into this project) — its curves, surfaces, modifiers and crowns come into a new group named after the file, sub-groups kept. Head, guides and meshes stay behind.
  • Presets (collapsible block at the top of Migrate): first the built-in examples — a click brings an example's whole hair in as one group; then yours: Choose folder… — where presets are kept (by default the program's System\Presets); ＋ Create preset — saves the group selected in the scene, with a picture of it; click a card to bring the preset in as its own group; ✕ deletes the preset file.

sections.title: Import head & meshes
sections.tags: import head model reference model character body obj glb gltf mesh meshes hat accessory polygroups wireframe wire imported transform mesh mask thickness
sections.body:
• + in the outliner → Head (the reference model the hair is drawn on) or Mesh → Imported (hat, accessory, body part…). Or drop the file on Import as head / Import as mesh.
  • Polygroups as separate meshes (in the + menu): every OBJ group / GLB mesh becomes a mesh of its own.
  • W in the outliner — the head's wireframe; ⬢ Wire on the top bar — imported meshes' wireframe.
  • Imported meshes move / rotate / scale with the gizmo (written into their Transform modifier); Mask and Thickness modifiers paint on them.

sections.title: Curves & anchors
sections.tags: copy ctrl+c clipboard glue snap to path link linked onto another curve curve curves draw drawing pencil line spline bezier anchor anchors point points handle handles weld unweld join connect merge split junction y branch fork roundness smoothing smooth even out optimize insert delete anchor sharp corner direction reverse flip root tip arrows snap slide along curve shift scissors cut split trim join diamond start
sections.body:
• Curve tool {k:draw}: click on the head / hair to place anchors; Enter finishes, Esc cancels.
  • RMB on a curve — insert an anchor (and drag it); RMB drag from empty space — a line: an anchor goes in wherever it crosses a curve (only the selected curves, if any are selected; the shape stays); B + LMB on an anchor — its smoothness (sharp ↔ smooth).
  • Weld: drag an anchor onto another → pie menu. A short curve welded to the middle of a long one becomes a Y branch (it continues along the long one's trunk). Ctrl + click a welded anchor of the selected curve — unweld.
  • Ctrl + drag — select / deselect anchors (curves welded along the touched segment come along).
  • Shift + RMB (pie): delete anchor / keep shape, recalculate handles, average curve, merge anchors at identical places, split at the anchor, rotate junction, create curve between two anchors, optimize anchors.
  • ∿ Create curve through the anchors: Shift + click anchors one by one, then Shift + RMB — a new curve through them in the order they were picked. It is free: new anchors at those places, welded and attached to nothing; it appears at the bottom of the outliner.
  • Properties: Roundness (0 — spline, 1 — circle arcs), Smoothing, Even out anchors (removes wobble). Double-click a slider's number to type a value.
  • Direction: a curve starts at its diamond anchor (the root) and runs to its tip. ⇄ Reverse direction (curve Settings or the pie with curves selected) swaps root and tip — modifiers then sweep from the other end (guide hits, connector attachments and painted weights stay in place).
  • Shift while dragging an anchor (or moving one anchor with the Move gizmo) — it snaps onto the curve nearest to the cursor (any group; that curve lights up cyan) and slides along it; bring the cursor to another curve to switch; release Shift to move freely again.
  • The first anchor of a curve (its start / root) is drawn as a diamond, the others as circles.
  • Scissors {k:cut}: RMB on a curve picks it (or select it before), then drag a line across it → pie: Split into two curves, Split, delete the upper part, Split, delete the lower part (upper — the piece whose free end is higher). The shape stays; welded curves along the cut are cut too; a wall between two cut curves is cut with them (cut the whole lock at once — it keeps its walls), a wall with only one of its curves cut is deleted.
  • Scissors → Split ends: click a curve where its end should split — from there to the tip it becomes a Y curve (the curve and a new branch sharing its trunk), the two ends spread apart (orange preview). The spread is set like a brush radius: Ctrl + RMB drag (or the Spread slider). A wall on one side of the curve stays with it, a wall on the other side goes over to the new branch; a tip shared with other curves splits too, each keeps the tip of its side. Click near an anchor — the split starts at that anchor.
  • Welding the start of one curve onto the end of another → pie: Reverse the curve whose start it is, then weld (the two ends meet), or Join into one curve — either way the curves are recalculated (clean automatic handles). Start + start or end + end — the usual weld.
  • Deleting the last own anchor of a Y branch (the rest runs along its host's trunk) deletes the branch — the host stays a single curve.
  • ⇶ Snap to path — a part of one lock's curve glued onto another lock's curve: select the target curve and copy it ({k:copySel} or ⧉ SEL), then select an anchor of the other curve → Shift + RMB → Snap to path → the Upper or the Lower part from that anchor (hover — the part and where it goes light up). Its anchors land on the target (the target gets anchors where needed) and stay linked in pairs: move either — both follow; the locks stay separate.

sections.title: Surfaces & locks
sections.tags: surface surfaces nurbs wall walls lock locks strand volume closed ring bulge width segments flip second surface unite locks junction fill hole gap segments to curves
sections.body:
• Select 2 curves → Shift + RMB → wall between them; 3+ curves → Volume lock (closed) — a ring of walls.
  • Wall properties: Width segments (Segment offset shifts the segment lines towards one curve; with 2+ lines Spread from centre moves them to the middle or to the edges), Bulge (bulges the wall out), Flip, Second surface (a lens-shaped lock from 2 curves), Segments → curves.
  • Pie with walls of 2+ locks: Unite locks (Y / X junction); with curves: Fill the hole between these curves, wall between two trunks.
  • ◧ NURBS on the top bar hides / shows all surfaces; its slider — their opacity.

sections.title: Move, rotate, scale (gizmo)
sections.tags: gizmo move rotate scale transform translate axis axes world local lock axis snap angle step uniform scale
sections.body:
• {k:move} Move, {k:rotate} Rotate, {k:gizmo} Scale — anchors, or whole objects / groups, discs, reference planes.
  • {k:gizmoSpace} — World / Local axes (like Cinema 4D: objects keep their own orientation).
  • {k:axisX} / {k:axisY} / {k:axisZ} — lock / unlock an axis.
  • Move arrows are grabbed anywhere inside a cone around them — narrow at the gizmo's centre, widening to the arrow tips. An axis pointing (almost) at the camera shows as a ring around the centre: drag there up / down (up — away from the camera); the centre itself stays the free move.
  • An axis pointing at the camera (Z in the Front view…) can also be dragged from the centre of the Move gizmo with Ctrl — it moves along that axis (mouse up — away from the camera). With the other two axes locked a plain drag from the centre does it.
  • Shift — rotation in 45° steps, scale in steps of 0.1; Ctrl — uniform scale.
  • Scale: the centre cube scales evenly — drag right / up for bigger, left / down for smaller (about ×2 per 170 px); a press near the gizmo's centre always takes the centre cube; an axis cube follows the pointer.

sections.title: Brush
sections.tags: brush sculpt shape push pull smooth smoothing inflate shrink thicker thinner radius size hardness strength screen surface
sections.body:
• Brush {k:brush}: drag over the hair to move anchors. Modes: Screen (everything inside the circle) / Surface (only what's near the touched point in 3D).
  • Shift — smooth; Ctrl — inflate the lock; Ctrl+Alt — shrink it.
  • With curves (or a disc) selected only they are affected.
  • {k:brushSmaller} / {k:brushBigger} — radius; Ctrl + RMB drag — radius / hardness.

sections.title: Guides (loop guides)
sections.tags: guide guides guide line disc nurbs disc loops loop direction ring rings cocoon density loop density influence radius blend on off switch disable enable power hidden
sections.body:
Guides work on cocoons only: a guide is a shell modifier of its cocoon (its child in the Cocoons section) and places one of its rings — the curves' own loops aren't touched.

  • Shell modifiers tool {k:guide} → Guidelines:
    • Line — select the cocoon, then drag a line across it: a ring of the cocoon lies in the line's plane there; the guide shows as that ring (green, yellow when selected). It keeps its place on the cocoon and follows it when the lock is edited; the cocoon stays selected for the next line. To move a guide: draw a new one, delete the old.
    • Where the cocoon takes the loops of its parent or of a linked cocoon, theirs rule: a guide on it there changes nothing (it says so) — put the guide on the parent instead.
    • NURBS disc — with a cocoon selected: click on it (or press Create) — a disc on that cocoon, a ring lies on it. With nothing selected: click (at that height) or Create — a level scene disc through all the cocoons (in the Guides group): a ring of every cocoon it crosses lies on it — the general alignment of all the locks (where a cocoon takes its parent's / a linked one's loops, theirs rule). A new disc starts switched off: place and shape it, then switch it on with ⏻ (a scene disc — in the outliner under Guides, a cocoon's — in the Cocoons section). E / R / T move, rotate, transform it; the Brush shapes it; Outer / Inner radius; Reset deformations; Select outer / inner ring — then E / R / T work on that ring only.
  • Influence radius — the zone along the cocoon round the guide where the rings turn toward its plane (while you drag or hover the slider: rings round the cocoon at the zone's edges and where Blend starts, the axis between). Blend — 0: the whole zone follows the guide, higher: weaker towards its edges.
  • Loop density — more rings in the zone (×1 — none added, the guide only turns them); it fades like Blend.
  • ⏻ in the outliner switches a guide on / off; hiding it (eye) switches it off too.
  • Also on the tool, Topology: Density and Parent influence painted along a cocoon (see Cocoons).

sections.title: Modifiers
sections.tags: modifier modifiers tube profile sweep shape mask thickness noise curl curls spiral cap caps close end fill holes extra weights paint pin tip tips tip density density denser sparser loops more fewer paint brush mask
sections.body:
• Modifier tool {k:modifier}: a tube along a curve with a profile (Quad, Trapezoid, Triangle, Circle… or your own); radius / rotation at start, middle, end; Convert to curves & walls.
  • Extra tab: Mask and Thickness (painted weights), Noise, Curls (spiral, density, anti-clipping).
  • Cap — closes the ends of closed locks (quads / point / tris, bevel). Fill — fills holes between curves of a group.
  • Density — more (or fewer) loops only where you paint it: add it to a group (Modifier tool → Topology → Density), set Density (×2 — twice as many loops, ×0.5 — half as many), then paint the curves of the locks with 🖌 Density brush (Ctrl — erase, Shift — smooth; the painted strength gives the density in between). Unpainted, it does nothing. The mask shows on the curves (dark — weak, yellow — full) while the tab is open or the modifier is selected; Clear mask removes it. Works on the locks of the group and its sub-groups; hide it (eye) to switch it off. (An old Tip density from earlier files becomes such a mask by itself — painted at the locks' tips.)
  • 📌 keeps the modifier menu on top while other tools are used.

sections.title: Crown
sections.tags: crown whorl parting part top of head connector cowlick
sections.body:
• Crown tool {k:crown}: click on the head where the whorl (back end of the parting) should be — a crown is built there from a template; ＋ Create fits it to the top of the head.
  • Crown curves end on the connectors; Ctrl + drag slides an attached anchor along the connector. Its mesh goes with the group's conversion.
  • Whorl (crown properties) — where many loops meet at one point of the parting line: Merge loops (default) — neighbouring loops merge in pairs below it (one triangle per merge), at most 2 reach the point; Seam on the crown curve — the loops next to the crown curve nearest the whorl end on it one by one, a herringbone seam along that curve.
  • The crown group's curves are shown like any group's (Auto — only while you work inside it); the connectors also show while anything is selected, so lock curves can be attached to them. Smart Rename names the crown curves Crown curve 1, 2 … along the lower connector.
  • Symmetric crown (mirror plane — the head's centre, X): new crowns are symmetric when Symmetric is ticked in the Crown tool. For an existing crown tick Symmetric in its properties and pick Left (+X) → Right (−X) or Right (−X) → Left (+X) — the character's own sides (it faces +Z: its left is +X) — that half is copied onto the other (the lower connector and the crown curves there are replaced, the parting line goes onto the middle; lock curves attached on that side stay). Then moving an anchor on either side moves its mirror. Crown curves added later aren't mirrored — ⇋ Mirror again…. Untick — both halves are free again.
  • Attach a lock curve to the lower connector: drag its end anchor onto the connector → ⛓ Attach. The anchor becomes a point of the connector — dragging it reshapes the connector (the curve follows); Ctrl + drag slides it along the connector; Ctrl + click (or Shift + RMB → Detach) detaches the curve — it gets its own anchor there, the connector keeps its shape.

sections.title: Edges & mesh → curves
sections.tags: edges edge edge loop loop selection path select edges mesh to curves convert mesh back curves from mesh retopo
sections.body:
• Edges tool {k:edge}: LMB — an edge, double-click — an edge loop, Shift — add, Ctrl — remove, Ctrl+Shift — path, Ctrl + box — deselect.
  • Shift + RMB: Convert the path to a curve. Mesh → curves & surfaces rebuilds a lock (curves + walls) from a mesh.

sections.title: Outliner & groups
sections.tags: outliner tree list hierarchy group groups folder parent unparent rename smart rename names sort colour color eye hide visibility labels label container separate topology exclude influence free curves symmetry mirror isolate group drag
sections.body:
• Groups nest; drag rows to move them; Shift / Ctrl + click, Ctrl + box to select; double-click a group — select everything inside.
  • {k:parent} parent to the last selected, {k:unparent} out of the hierarchy, {k:rename} rename, {k:smartRename} Smart Rename (tidy names, prefixes, find & replace, sort).
  • Group row: 🏷 labels, guide mode A / ∿ / ⌀, colour swatch (double-click — reset), ⏻ guides on / off, 👁 eye.
  • Labels: Free curves visible; a crown's group — Connectors visible. (Groups never line their loops up with each other — every lock is built on its own.)
  • Group symmetry: a live mirror copy; Apply symmetry makes it real.

sections.title: Cocoons (◍)
sections.tags: link links linked alt drag dependency depend cocoon cocoons shell shells ring rings loops lock locks strand strands trunk branch branches tree make create button toolbar what is how works on the lock on the cocoon projection projected opacity hide show density even loops guideline guidelines line disc shell modifiers
sections.body:
A cocoon is a see-through shell round a lock (its curves and walls). It shows where the lock's loops go — its rings, spaced by the loop step and Deviation of the lock's group (closer on bends) — and lets you shape them. It has no curves of its own and doesn't change the hair: it is a guide for the loops. (Convert doesn't read the rings yet — it places the loops by itself.)

Making one

  • Select a lock — its group, its curves or its walls — and press ◍ Cocoon in the left toolbar (section Cocoons).
  • The cocoon follows the lock: move its anchors and the cocoon reshapes. It keeps the lock's strands (paths root → tip) it was made from; branches added to the lock later stay out of it.
  • A lock that splits into branches: the cocoon goes round its main branch (where most strands end); the other branches are left out — make cocoons of them too. A side branch that keeps beside the main one and runs on past the cocoon's tip only a little (up to 4 loop steps — a tip split in two) needs none: it takes its neighbour's loops, on to its own tip at the same spacing.
  • A cocoon selected together with the lock — the new one becomes its branch. Otherwise, if the new cocoon starts inside another one's shell, it becomes that one's branch by itself; else it is a trunk.

In the outliner and the viewport

  • The Cocoons section of the outliner (◍ in the outliner header folds it): trunks and their branches as a tree. Drag a cocoon onto another — it becomes its branch; onto empty space — a trunk of its own. Or with keys: select cocoons, then the parent cocoon last → {k:parent}; a branch → {k:unparent} — a trunk of its own. {k:smartRename} renames cocoons too (a selected cocoon — with its branches).
  • A new cocoon is named after its lock (LeftTail_09 cocoon), a branch too. Where a name doesn't say its lock (older ones: … · branch · branch), the lock is shown dim in front of it. Selecting a lock (its group, a curve, a wall, an anchor) lights its cocoon; when it sits in a folded branch, that folded cocoon is pale orange.
  • The shell shows while the cocoon is selected; its rings stay on the lock.
  • 👁 hides the cocoon — the rings on the lock stay; ◎ next to it hides the rings.

Settings (select the cocoon)

  • Rings: On the lock (new cocoons) — projected onto the lock's walls, as the loops will lie on the hair; On the cocoon — drawn on the shell.
  • Opacity of the shell (double-click — the default).
  • Denser on bends and Denser to the tip — how much closer the rings come on bends (full on a bend of 30° a loop step) and over the last stretch toward the tip: ×1 — no closer, by default ×2 on bends and ×1.5 to the tip (double-click — back to it).
  • The number of rings and the loop step; trunk or branch; the strands it follows.
  • A branch takes its parent's rings where it runs inside the parent and turns to its own spacing over 3 loop steps after it leaves.
  • 🔗 Link — a cocoon that also crosses another cocoon besides its parent (e.g. its trunk's branch) takes that one's loops too, where it runs inside it: in the Cocoons section hold Alt and drag from the cocoon to the other one. The link shows as an orange line with an arrow on the left of the rows; Alt + click on the line breaks it. Where the parent and a linked cocoon give a loop at one place, the parent's stays. A link that would go round in a circle (that cocoon takes loops from this one) isn't made.

Shaping the rings — Shell modifiers ({k:guide})

  • Density — paint along a cocoon: more (or fewer) rings there. Ctrl+Shift — its second mode, Even spacing (cyan): the rings there equally apart — bends and the tip don't crowd them; Ctrl+Shift+Alt — erase it. Shift smooths both masks.
  • Parent influence — a mask painted along a cocoon, like Thickness: LMB weakens the pull of its parent (and linked cocoons) — red; where weakened enough, the cocoon spaces its own rings even inside them. Ctrl — inverted, adds it — green: the cocoon takes their loops further out, beside them too. Ctrl+Alt — erase, Shift — smooth.
  • Line — drag a line across the lock's curves: a ring lies along it. Several cocoons selected (or curves of several locks) — one stroke makes a guide on each of them, linked: 🔗N beside them in the Cocoons section (hover — the others light up, click — selects them all); Linked settings in a guide's settings — on, its Influence radius, Blend and Loop density go with the others'; off — set on its own.
  • NURBS disc — click on a cocoon (or select it and press Create): a ring lies on the disc; move, rotate or brush it.
  • Each modifier is listed under its cocoon in the Cocoons section (👁 — switch it off).
  • ⏻ on the Cocoons header — all the shell modifiers off at once (Density, Parent influence, guide lines, discs — on cocoons and in the scene): the rings as with none; click again — back, each as it was. Kept in the project, Ctrl+Z undoes it.

sections.title: Loops & conversion to mesh
sections.tags: convert conversion mesh bake baked loops loop step spacing density deviation fix sharp angles horizontal perpendicular orientation tips point gradual relax merge shared trunks quads triangles topology extract geometry export obj confirm cancel preview y junction fork anchors count narrow strip
sections.body:
• Convert to geometry window (right column): it lists the selected cocoons (a parent with its branches selected — as their tree); Loop step and Deviation — the spacing of their rings. Auto weld points (On by default): points closer than the Weld distance become one (auto — a quarter of the loop step, ◎ Pick — measure it; smaller at the tips; a tip goes into a point only on a lock with no thickness — one surface). It joins what is apart — cracks between walls, loose ends; points near each other in the mesh (one face, or a neighbour in common) are never welded, so narrow roots and tips keep their faces. Weld locks: where a child (or linked) cocoon runs into its parent's — its root inside it, where it enters and where it leaves it — its lock is welded to the parent's: the row of the child's mesh there must lie on one loop of the parent's (within the weld distance); then the two become one mesh, the joint's points welded onto that loop. Check connections shows the joints: red — no room for the joint (its edge doesn't land on a loop of the parent), green — fine; with Weld locks on, Convert checks them by itself and names the ones it couldn't weld. Convert — each selected cocoon's lock becomes a mesh by its rings: its loops are the rings you see on the lock (a ring goes on a wall where it crosses all of that wall), the root and the tip close it; the faces are turned to agree with each other and to face out (the normals checked by themselves). The meshes go straight into Meshes, the converted locks' walls and curves are hidden; Ctrl+Z — all back. The meshes go into the Meshes group at the top of the outliner by themselves. ⭳ Export ▾ — the meshes as OBJ / glTF / PLY / STL; 🔗 Bridge ▾ + ⇪ Send — straight into Blender, Maya or a watched folder.
  • Loop step — spacing of loops (Set reference); Deviation — how much a loop's size may differ from the step by the curvature (step 10, Deviation 50% → loops 5…15); Fix sharp angles (on by default) — turns sharp diagonal loops back towards square (narrow strips first); Loops: horiz. ↔ perp.; Tips (Point / Gradual); Relax loop spacing; Merge shared trunks (welded locks become one surface).
  • Loop count comes from the step, not from the anchors; only a Y junction (an anchor where two curves of a lock that ran together part) places a loop — right through it, unless a guide with Priority 50%+ rules there (in locks welded to other locks the shared trunks' loops rule).
  • Every lock is built on its own: only its group's settings and the guides shape it; locks welded along a trunk share its loops one to one. Clean topology on a surface — straight, parallel loops there. The Tip modifier makes the tips denser.

sections.title: Reference images
sections.tags: reference references image images picture photo board pureref plane planes background concept art front view side view orthographic ortho follow camera pivot opacity crop mirror copy duplicate other view opposite move canvas ctrl alt proportional
sections.body:
• 🖼 Reference ▾: the reference board — a free window over the viewport (like PureRef): import / paste / drop images, move, scale, rotate, crop (C), mirror (H), opacity, lock.
  • Planes: an image placed in a view (Front / Back / Left / Right / Top) behind the model; move / rotate / scale it with the gizmo (scaling by a two-axis square keeps the picture's proportions, Ctrl — free), pivot lock, Centre, Over the model, Only in its view. Ctrl + Alt + LMB drag moves the active plane's canvas whatever is under the pointer. ⧉ Copy to — a copy of the plane for another view (same image, size and place on the model); into the opposite view (Right ↔ Left, Front ↔ Back, marked ⇋) the picture is mirrored. An Orthographic plane is for the free Orthographic view: it follows the camera — orbit around the model and the image stays in front of you, where you put it (everything else works as with the other planes). Place and scale it on the model with the gizmo, then tick 📌 Lock to the model: panning and zooming keep the image on the model, only orbiting can put the view off — ↩ Locked view brings the view of that moment back.

sections.title: Hotkeys
sections.tags: hotkeys hotkey shortcuts shortcut keyboard keys key bindings keymap change keys
sections.body:
Change them in ⌨ Hotkeys above the viewport. They work in any keyboard layout.

{k:__ACTIONS__}__
Esccancel / deselect
Enterfinish the curve
B + LMBanchor smoothness
Shift + RMBpie menu

sections.title: Rooms: Hair and Topology
sections.tags: room rooms switch hair topology retopology workspace mode tab scene separate own outliner undo history what is shared
sections.body:
The switch next to ⌨ Hotkeys (above the viewport) changes the room — the program's workspace for one kind of work. The room you are in shows its name, the other one only its icon.

  • ✂ Hair — the main room: curves, NURBS walls, locks, cocoons, conversion into the hair mesh.
  • ▦ Topology — retopology: its own outliner, logic and tools (they come one by one with the next updates).

What each room has of its own

  • Its scene: the items in its outliner.
  • Its undo history ({k:undo} / {k:redo} step only through the room you are in), its selection, its active tool.
  • Its toolbar and its FAQ (this window shows the sections of the room you are in).

Shared by the rooms

  • The head (reference model), the camera, the reference board and planes, the 👁 Display settings.

Nothing moves from one room into the other yet. Both rooms are saved in the same project file; a project always opens in the Hair room.

sections.title: The Topology room
sections.tags: topology retopology retopo room start begin overview what is new mesh low poly quads tools toolbar empty start here navigation camera orbit pan zoom
sections.body:
The Topology room is for retopology. It has its own logic, outliner and tools — none of the Hair room's tools are carried over.

Here now

  • The room's own outliner (narrow, one tree) and its own undo history. Meshes are shared with the Hair room.
  • Modes — the strip left of the outliner: Object, Polygon, Edge, Vertex. The selected mesh is drawn in the mode's look: polygons purple in front and orange behind, the edges dark, the vertices black (white when selected).
  • Cursor: LMB — an element of the mode, Shift — add, Ctrl — deselect (drag — a box), double click — the loop (a polygon inside a closed frame of selected polygons — the whole area inside), Ctrl+Shift — the shortest path (in the Object mode — the polygroup under the cursor: it lights up while the keys are held, a click picks it, again — unpicks), drag on empty space — a box. LMB held on an element and dragged — moves it across the screen. Esc or Ctrl+D — deselect; Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y — the selection steps too.
  • Move / Rotate / Scale — the gizmo, on the selected meshes or on the selected polygons / edges / vertices. The tools are in a floating window (drag its bar; double-click — a row / a column).
  • Under the modes: Snap — the vertices being edited stick to the other meshes' surface (only those); Symmetry — an edit mirrored onto the vertices' pairs across the mesh's X = 0; 🖌 — the snap mask brush.
  • Snap mask (a mesh's settings): pick polygroups (Ctrl+Shift in the Object mode, or in the list), From the picked polygroups — vertices then snap only to them; Leave out the covered parts drops what another layer of the mesh covers. The brush (a tool of its own — Q Q switches it and the Cursor) mends it: LMB adds, Ctrl erases, [ / ] — size; a layer under another isn't painted; with Symmetry on — mirrored. Mirror +X → −X / −X → +X copies one side's mask onto the other (across the mesh's X = 0); RMB on a polygroup → Remove from the snap mask. Brush: Shift + drag — a lasso adding, Shift + Ctrl — erasing; Paint through — the hidden parts too. Mask on off — the mask is kept but not used.
  • Ctrl+H with polygroups picked: only they are shown (the other groups and meshes hidden); Ctrl+H again — everything back.
  • Polygroup list: Ctrl / Shift — pick several, Ctrl+G — into a folder, F2 — rename, drag onto a row's middle — make it a child, onto its edge — before / after.
  • 👁 Display (this room's own): Wire on / off; Smooth, Flat, Unlit (no lighting), No textures; Opacity of the active (selected) geometry; PDO — the active geometry drawn nearer the camera so it covers the mesh under it (a retopology over its reference).
  • Transform table (in the right column, under Settings): position, rotation, size; units (cm by default). Ctrl + drag on a number — ±1, Ctrl+Shift — ±0.1; drag across cells — select them, then type one number for all.
  • ＋ Import: as the head (or added to it), polygroups on / off — as polygroups or as separate meshes. A heavy model is offered decimation; identical parts (mirrored eyes, boots…) are decimated the same way.
  • Settings of a mesh: its polygroups (drag to reorder, 👁 hide, ⧉ duplicate, ✕ delete, double click — select it, RMB — detach, merge, border, move the selected polygons in, identical / symmetric parts), then Material, textures, Use as reference (not pickable), Wire, Smooth / Flat.
  • The head (reference model), the camera and the references — shared with the Hair room.
